text:
Alice M: heads-up — seeing a wave of GPU pod evictions in us-west2 this morning. lots of small jobs stuck in Pending until another node frees, then mass evict when probe flaps. :(
Björn L: any errors in kubelet logs / node status?
Alice M: Node condition flips to NotReady for ~20s repeatedly. kubelet shows `Failed to list pods` then `network probe failed` before it recovers. snippet:
```
Aug 03 08:41:12 node-uw2-gpu-14 kubelet[1234]: E0803 08:41:12 watcher.go:56] watch chan error: net/http: TLS handshake timeout
Aug 03 08:41:32 node-uw2-gpu-14 kubelet[1234]: I0803 08:41:32 NodeStatus: Ready
```
Carmen P: that lines up with the autoscaler / nodepool churn we rolled last night. we bumped `maxUnavailable` on the kube-proxy DaemonSet for faster upgrades — could be transient conn disruption.
Mike R: also seeing fragmentation: many nodes with 1 GPU free but requests require 2 GPUs, so scheduler keeps bouncing pods.
SRE Oncall: confirmed increased eviction rate in the dashboard — roughly 80 evictions / hour on that zone since 06:00. cost spike from retries + fallback to dedicated pools.
Alice M: current behavior: 1) probe flaps -> node NotReady -> pods go to Terminating -> scheduler reschedules -> ends up on other nodes causing pressure -> many short-lived evictions.
Laura S: do we have pod topology/affinity for these workloads? most are ML jobs with `podAntiAffinity` preferredAcrossHosts to avoid noisy neighbors. That makes packing worse.
Björn L: suggestion: temporarily relax anti-affinity on best-effort workloads so they can share GPUs and lower fragmentation. add a low-weight PreferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution rule.
Carmen P: +1. Also think we should run a targeted descheduler job for that ASG to consolidate 1-GPU leftovers into fewer nodes. e.g. run `RemoveDuplicates` and `LowNodeUtilization` policies with GPU-weighted thresholds.
SRE Oncall: would need a short maintenance window to run descheduler — risk of extra evictions. prefer running during low-traffic window (13:00 UTC).
Mike R: alternative: allow scheduler to consider fractional GPU packing via k8s Device Plugin that supports MIG/shared GPUs? Not trivial for current images.
Alice M: immediate mitigation plan proposed:
- revert the kube-proxy change that increased `maxUnavailable` to reduce probe noise (Carmen to rollback)
- add a temporary SchedulerProfile tweak: prefer packing by GPU count (score plugin weight up) for the us-west2 profile
- schedule descheduler run off-peak to consolidate leftovers
- bump priorityClass for long-running training jobs to avoid preemption loops
Carmen P: rolling back the kube-proxy change now. Deploy Bot: deploy started by Carmen P at 08:45 — status: success :white_check_mark:
Deploy Bot: rolling-update daemonset kube-proxy -> maxUnavailable: 1 (reverted)
Björn L: for the scheduler profile tweak, here's a config snippet we can test in canary cluster:
```
policy: "PredicatesAndPriority"
pluginConfig:
  - name: "MostAllocated"
    args:
      resourceWeights:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 50
```
Laura S: we'll need to watch latency SLOs if we force tighter packing — risk increased queueing. set an alert to revert if 95p latency > 300ms for 10m.
Mike R: I'll open a quick runbook checklist for the descheduler job and the canary scheduler change. linking it here: https://internal.redwood/ops/descheduler-playbook
SRE Oncall: monitoring rule created: `us-west2.gpu.evictions > 50 / 10m` -> page SRE Oncall.
Alice M: thanks. owners: Carmen = kube-proxy rollback (done), Björn = scheduler pack canary + metrics, Mike = descheduler runbook + job, Laura = latency watch. We'll sync after the canary results at 13:10 UTC. :thumbsup:
Björn L: one longer-term item: schedule a capacity defrag run (reserve transient buffer to allow 2-GPU scheduling) and assess cost trade-offs. add to quarterly infra backlog.
Carmen P: noted. also let's audit any DaemonSet/Pod disruption changes we made last month that touch networking.
Laura S: thanks all. ping me if the canary looks bad and we'll roll back.
Alice M: closing the immediate alert for now, will reopen if evictions persist. :lock:
